s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic skin lesions with slow growth, associated with neurological deficits and family history of similar conditions
salient_findings: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
key_facts: Female patient in her early 50s
Lesions on the lower legs have been growing slowly since age 24
Lesions have been bleeding occasionally after trauma
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
Patient had an intracranial hemorrhage
Patient had recurrent seizures at age 4
Lipolymphedema of the lower legs is attributed to functional venous insufficiency
Patient has been wearing compression stockings for years
Family history of similar conditions in the patient's father and aunt
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations
Histopathology revealed a well-circumscribed lesion with hyperkeratosis and acanthosis
Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

shortlist.label: Cerebral Cavernous Malformations (CCM)
shortlist.why_kept: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant and family history of similar conditions

shortlist.label: Familial cerebral cavernous malformations
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar conditions and presence of intracranial hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Blue Rubber Bleb Nevus Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Lipolymphedema of the lower legs and presence of vascular malformations

shortlist.label: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of similar conditions and presence of vascular malformations

raw.rationale: The patient's family history of similar conditions, including the father's death from an intracranial hemorrhage, combined with the detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, strongly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cerebral Cavernous Malformations (CCM)
rejected.why: While CCM is a possible diagnosis, the familial aspect and genetic testing results make familial cerebral cavernous malformations a more specific and accurate diagnosis.

rejected.label: Blue Rubber Bleb Nevus Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with intestinal lesions and a distinct set of skin manifestations, which do not fully align with the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves port-wine stains, varicose veins, and bony and soft tissue hypertrophy, which are not the primary features in this patient's case.

rejected.label: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations, particularly in the lungs, liver, and brain, which do not match the patient's specific vascular malformations and symptoms.
